{"body":"Part of #35 (section 5 publish learnings + section 6 placeholder pattern; per the maintainer's decision, DOCUMENTED RECIPES for humans and agents — not CLI machinery).

## The picture

A whole class of failure has one signature: **the build succeeds, and the upload doesn't run.** No compiler error, no test failure — the defect exists only on itch's CDN, or only inside a `.app` bundle, or only on someone else's clone. You cannot unit-test your way to these; you can only KNOW them. *Witch v Necromancer* paid for six. They become one recipe page.

## The six, each with its "why it passes locally"

1. **Verify before push.** A publish script must ASSERT what the platform needs — relative `<base href>`, `index.html` at the upload root, `Content/` genuinely populated (the content build is a separate MSBuild path that can no-op while the build reports success), interop shims resolving, mac arch matching the RID with a valid signature — because each fails only after upload.
2. **Test the web build at a SUBPATH.** `python3 -m http.server` serves from a root — the one layout itch never uses — so it passes while the real upload 404s every `_framework/` fetch. The recipe's test server mounts at `/html/<id>/` like itch does and prints every 404.
3. **`ExcludeAssets="all"` on content-pipeline PackageReferences.** Without it a shipped mac game carries **~25 MB of authoring toolchain** — libassimp, FFmpeg, the D3D shader compiler — tools for BUILDING content inside a game that only READS it. MGCB runs out-of-process from the NuGet cache, so the content build is unaffected. Verify against a cleared `Content/bin`.
4. **Codesign ORDER.** `codesign` pointed inside `.app/Contents/MacOS` adopts the whole bundle and dies on what sits beside the executable (`.anim` art folders read as malformed nested bundles; managed DLLs as unsigned code objects). Sign the PLAIN publish-dir executable BEFORE bundling. Apple Silicon refuses unsigned arm64 outright — hard gate, not cosmetics.
   Bonus trap from the same script, worth its paragraph: under `set -o pipefail`, a verification pipeline whose consumer exits early (`grep -q`, `head -n`) kills the producer with SIGPIPE (exit 141) and a PASSING check reads as FAILING. Capture output into a variable and match it.
5. **Prune Blazor's `*.br`/`*.gz` for itch.** itch does not negotiate `Content-Encoding`; the precompressed variants are a third of the upload nobody downloads — 28 MB → 19 MB by deletion.
6. **The licensed-content placeholder pattern.** Gitignored licensed audio + MGCB's hard failure on missing inputs = a public repo NOBODY can build (proven: five hard errors on a fresh clone). The pattern: a committed placeholder substituted at build time for any absent track (list derived from the `.mgcb` itself; a real file is never overwritten); a warning that fires on EVERY build by HASHING against the placeholder — a marker file goes stale, and a stale marker is a mute release nobody was warned about; and a publish gate that refuses to package a placeholder.

## Delivery

- [ ] One recipe page (e.g. `docs/recipes/shipping.md`) covering the six, each with the failure signature, the why-it-passes-locally, and the countermeasure
- [ ] Point at the reference implementations to adapt: `roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj` → `tools/publish-itch.sh`, `tools/serve-web-build.py`, `Gmtk2026.Core/Content/MusicPlaceholders.targets`, `tools/build-placeholder-track.py`
- [ ] Cross-link from the web-targeting docs and the CLI template (#55) so the page is findable at the moment of need

Pure documentation — no code lands in the engine.

**Value on its own:** the six production-only failures stop being tuition every project pays separately. An agent (or a human) shipping a MonoDreams game reads one page instead of rediscovering each the expensive way.
","comments":[],"labels":[],"title":"docs: shipping recipes — the six failures that only exist in production (itch, codesign, placeholders)"}

# Web targeting (KNI / BlazorGL)

MonoDreams games can ship to the **web browser** (Chrome latest, WebGL) in
addition to desktop. The web backend is [KNI](https://github.com/kniEngine/kni),
a MonoGame-compatible fork whose **BlazorGL** platform runs on WebAssembly.

The key fact that makes this cheap: KNI keeps the same
`Microsoft.Xna.Framework` *namespace* but ships under different *assembly
identities* (`nkast.Xna.Framework.*`). So **MonoDreams' own source recompiles
unchanged** against either backend — only *precompiled* third-party
dependencies need a KNI-built variant.

> **Read first** if you are changing engine source: `docs/CORE_TENETS.md`,
> and the premises that govern this seam —
> `MonoDreams/foundation/docs/premises.md` ("Engine source is
> backend/OS-agnostic", "The platform … is selected by the head project"),
> `MonoDreams/level-loading/docs/premises.md` ("Content is built per-platform
> … processors must match the backend's pipeline assemblies"), and
> `MonoDreams/level-ldtk/docs/premises.md` ("LDtkMonogame is vendored as
> source").

## The project model: shared `.Core` + per-platform heads

A multi-platform game is **one shared game library plus one head per
platform**, never a single project that hard-codes a backend:

```
MyGame.Core/      shared game code + MonoDreams modules (platform-agnostic).
                  Backend chosen by the $(MonoDreamsPlatform) MSBuild property.
MyGame.Desktop/   DesktopGL head: Program.cs -> new Game(); game.Run().
                  References MonoGame.Framework.DesktopGL.
MyGame.Web/       BlazorGL head: just WebGame.cs + a one-line Program.cs +
                  wwwroot/index.html. All other host wiring comes from the shared
                  MonoDreams.Web.Hosting library (below).
MyGame.sln        the desktop heads build by default; the web head is excluded
                  (see "Why the web head is excluded from the .sln build").
```

The reference app `MonoDreams.Examples` is laid out exactly this way —
`MonoDreams.Examples.Core` + `.Desktop` + `.Web` — and doubles as the template
the CLI generates.

Every web head is a Blazor WASM host with the *same* boot wiring: install the
web `IPlatformServices`, build the `WebAssemblyHostBuilder`, mount a full-window
`<canvas>`, and drive `Game.Tick()` from a `requestAnimationFrame` loop. That
wiring lives **once** in `MonoDreams.Web.Hosting` (a Razor Class Library), so a
head carries only what is genuinely its own:

## The task (GitHub issue #56)
Create ONE new file: `docs/recipes/shipping.md`.

It documents "the six failures that only exist in production" — a class of failure whose signature is: **the build succeeds, and the defect only appears after upload** (on itch.io's CDN, inside a mac `.app` bundle, or on someone else's clone). You cannot unit-test your way to these; they must be known. The reference game *Witch v Necromancer* (repo roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj, public) paid for all six; this page turns them into recipes so no MonoDreams project pays that tuition again.

Each of the six recipes must have three parts: **the failure signature** (what you observe in production), **why it passes locally**, and **the countermeasure** (what to assert/do, pointing at the reference implementation to adapt).

The six, from the issue:

276	      || die "the bundled executable differs from the signed one — cp did not carry the signature in"

291	# warning says so, but a warning scrolls past in a wall of MSBuild output and a push does not.

308	      silent+=("$track")
309	    fi
310	  done < <(sed -n 's|^#begin \(Music/.*\)$|\1|p' "$manifest")

312	  if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 || ${#silent[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
313	    die "the music in this tree is not shippable.
314	    ${#silent[@]} silent placeholder(s): ${silent[*]:-none}
315	    ${#missing[@]} absent (the build would substitute silence): ${missing[*]:-none}
316	    Restore the real tracks with tools/clip-music.py — Content/ATTRIBUTION.md records the master and
317	    the exact arguments for each one. A build with these in it is mute, and nothing downstream says so."
318	  fi
319	  note "music          $(sed -n 's|^#begin Music/||p' "$manifest" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') licensed track(s) present, none placeholder"
320	}
321	
322	# ============================================================================ run
323	say "Preflight"
324	assert_real_music
325	[[ $do_web -eq 1 ]] && stage_web
326	if [[ $do_mac -eq 1 ]]; then
327	  for rid in "${MAC_RIDS[@]}"; do stage_mac "$rid"; done
328	fi
329	
330	if [[ $DO_PUSH -eq 1 ]]; then
331	  [[ -n "$TARGET" ]] || die "--push needs --target <user>/<game> (or ITCH_TARGET)"
332	  command -v "$BUTLER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ -x "$BUTLER" ]] || die "butler not found at '$BUTLER'"

334	  if [[ $do_mac -eq 1 ]]; then
335	    for rid in "${MAC_RIDS[@]}"; do push_channel "$STAGE_ROOT/$rid" "$rid"; done
336	  fi
337	  say "Pushed: ${PUSHED_CHANNELS[*]}"
338	  for channel in "${PUSHED_CHANNELS[@]}"; do
339	    echo "    $BUTLER status $TARGET:$channel"
340	  done

342	  say "Packaged, not pushed"
343	  cat <<EOF
344	    Push with:
345	      tools/publish-itch.sh --skip-build --push --target roooliv/witch-v-necromancer
346	
347	    Page settings butler cannot set (once per project):
348	      - Kind of project:  HTML   (else the web upload is offered as a download, not played)
349	      - Embed size:       1280 x 720
350	EOF
351	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# publish-itch.sh — build, verify and push this game's itch.io uploads.
#
# Channels:
#   html5        the KNI/BlazorGL web head, played in the browser
#   osx-arm64    macOS .app bundle, Apple Silicon
#   osx-x64      macOS .app bundle, Intel
#
# Package (local and reversible — touches nothing outside the repo):
#   tools/publish-itch.sh                      # every channel
#   tools/publish-itch.sh --only web
#   tools/publish-itch.sh --only mac
#   tools/publish-itch.sh --only web --serve    # + boot the web build at an itch-like subpath
#   tools/publish-itch.sh --only web --zip      # + a zip for manual dashboard upload
#
# Publish (outward-facing, so it is opt-in):
#   tools/publish-itch.sh --push --target roooliv/witch-v-necromancer
#
# Each channel is verified before it can be pushed, because every failure mode below produces a
# BUILD THAT SUCCEEDS and an upload that does not run:
#
#   web  * <base href> must be RELATIVE. itch serves from html-classic.itch.zone/html/<build-id>/,
#          so "/" points the Blazor loader at the CDN root and every _framework/ fetch 404s.
#        * index.html must sit at the upload root — itch opens <root>/index.html and nothing else.
#        * Content/ must hold real assets. The KNI content build is a separate MSBuild path from the
#          C# compile; it can no-op while the build reports success, and the game then boots and
#          throws on its first Load<Texture2D>.
#        * The nkast.Wasm.* JS interop shims are hand-versioned in index.html and hard-coupled to the
#          restored package version; a bump 404s them at runtime with no build-time warning.
#   mac  * The bundle must be Contents/MacOS/<CFBundleExecutable> with the exec bit intact, or macOS
#          reports a damaged application.
#        * A bundle launches with CWD=/, so anything resolving content relative to the working
#          directory dies. This game resolves from AppDomain.BaseDirectory only (verified), which is
#          Contents/MacOS — where the publish output and its Content/ go.
#
# PIPEFAIL HAZARD, learned the hard way: with `pipefail`, a consumer that exits early (grep -q, head -n)
# closes the pipe, the producer dies of SIGPIPE (exit 141), and the whole pipeline reports failure — so a
# passing check reads as a failing one. This script's signature check did exactly that: it aborted a
# perfectly signed build with "not signed", and the same command run by hand (no pipefail) passed, which
# sent the diagnosis chasing codesign's bundle behaviour instead. Verify by CAPTURING output into a
# variable and matching it, or with a single process that reads the file itself.
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

WEB_PROJECT="Gmtk2026.Web"
DESKTOP_PROJECT="Gmtk2026.Desktop"
WEB_PUBLISH="$WEB_PROJECT/bin/Release/net8.0/publish/wwwroot"
STAGE_ROOT="artifacts/itch"

APP_NAME="Witch v Necromancer"
BUNDLE_ID="io.itch.roooliv.witch-v-necromancer"
EXECUTABLE="Gmtk2026.Desktop"
MAC_RIDS=("osx-arm64" "osx-x64")

TARGET="${ITCH_TARGET:-}"
BUTLER="${BUTLER:-butler}"
ONLY=""
SKIP_BUILD=0
DO_PUSH=0
DO_ZIP=0
DO_SERVE=0

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --only)       ONLY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --target)     TARGET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --butler)     BUTLER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --skip-build) SKIP_BUILD=1; shift ;;
    --push)       DO_PUSH=1; shift ;;
    --zip)        DO_ZIP=1; shift ;;
    --serve)      DO_SERVE=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)    sed -n '2,40p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

[[ -z "$ONLY" || "$ONLY" == "web" || "$ONLY" == "mac" ]] || { echo "--only takes web|mac" >&2; exit 2; }
do_web=1; do_mac=1
[[ "$ONLY" == "mac" ]] && do_web=0
[[ "$ONLY" == "web" ]] && do_mac=0

say()  { printf '\n\033[1m==> %s\033[0m\n' "$*"; }
note() { printf '    %s\n' "$*"; }
die()  { printf '\n\033[1;31mFAIL: %s\033[0m\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

PUSHED_CHANNELS=()

# A build label that ties an itch build back to a commit. A dirty tree is marked as such: "it worked
# on the build page" is worth nothing if you cannot tell which tree produced it.
version_label() {
  local sha dirty
  sha=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)
  dirty=$([[ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]] && echo "-dirty" || echo "")
  echo "0.1.0+${sha}${dirty}"
}

push_channel() {                                  # push_channel <dir> <channel>
  local dir="$1" channel="$2" version
  version=$(version_label)
  say "Pushing $dir -> $TARGET:$channel (userversion $version)"
  "$BUTLER" push "$dir" "$TARGET:$channel" --userversion "$version"
  PUSHED_CHANNELS+=("$channel")
}

# ============================================================================ web
stage_web() {
  local stage="$STAGE_ROOT/html5"

  if [[ $SKIP_BUILD -eq 0 ]]; then
    say "Building $WEB_PROJECT (Release, web backend)"
    # MonoDreamsPlatform must be GLOBAL (-p:) so it reaches restore through the project graph — see
    # Gmtk2026.Web.csproj. Build the desktop head at least once first: the web content build borrows
    # native FreeImage/freetype from the cached dotnet-mgcb tool.
    dotnet publish "$WEB_PROJECT" -c Release -p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web
  fi
  [[ -d "$WEB_PUBLISH" ]] || die "no web publish output at $WEB_PUBLISH — drop --skip-build"

  say "Staging web -> $stage"
  rm -rf "$stage"; mkdir -p "$stage"
  cp -a "$WEB_PUBLISH/." "$stage/"          # trailing /. so index.html lands at the stage ROOT

  # Blazor emits pre-compressed copies for servers that negotiate Content-Encoding. itch does not, so
  # the loader fetches the plain files and these are dead weight — a THIRD of the upload, downloaded
  # by nobody. web.config is IIS hosting config, meaningless here.
  local pruned
  pruned=$(find "$stage" -type f \( -name '*.br' -o -name '*.gz' \) | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  find "$stage" -type f \( -name '*.br' -o -name '*.gz' \) -delete
  rm -f "$stage/web.config"
  note "pruned $pruned pre-compressed file(s) + web.config"

  say "Verifying web upload"
  [[ -f "$stage/index.html" ]] || die "index.html is not at the upload root"

  local base_href
  # One awk over the file rather than grep|head|sed: `head -1` closes the pipe on the first match and
  # SIGPIPEs grep, which `set -o pipefail` then reports as a failure (see the note at the top).
  base_href=$(awk 'match($0, /<base href="[^"]*"/) {
      s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/.*href="/, "", s); sub(/"$/, "", s); print s; exit }' \
    "$stage/index.html")
  [[ -n "$base_href" ]] || die "no <base href> in index.html — Blazor cannot resolve _framework/"
  [[ "$base_href" != /* ]] || die "<base href=\"$base_href\"> is ABSOLUTE. itch serves from a subpath, so
      every _framework/ fetch will 404 and the game will never boot. Use \"./\" in
      $WEB_PROJECT/wwwroot/index.html."
  note "base href      $base_href (relative — resolves under itch's /html/<id>/ subpath)"

  [[ -f "$stage/_framework/blazor.boot.json" ]] || die "_framework/blazor.boot.json missing"
  [[ -f "$stage/_framework/dotnet.native.wasm" ]] || die "_framework/dotnet.native.wasm missing"

  local content_files
  content_files=$(find "$stage/Content" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [[ "$content_files" -gt 10 ]] || die "Content/ has only $content_files file(s) — the KNI content build
      did not run. The game will boot and then throw on its first asset load."
  note "content        $content_files built asset(s)"

  local missing=0 shim
  while read -r shim; do

  [[ $missing -eq 0 ]] || die "$missing interop shim(s) referenced by index.html are absent. The
      nkast.Wasm.* version in index.html's script srcs no longer matches the restored packages."
  note "interop shims  all present"
  note "upload         $(find "$stage" -type f | wc -l | tr -d ' ') files, $(du -sh "$stage" | cut -f1 | tr -d ' ')"

  if [[ $DO_ZIP -eq 1 ]]; then
    say "Zipping web build for manual upload"
    local zip_path="$STAGE_ROOT/gmtk2026-html5.zip"
    rm -f "$zip_path"
    ( cd "$stage" && zip -qr "$REPO_ROOT/$zip_path" . )   # from INSIDE, so index.html is at the zip root
    note "$zip_path ($(du -h "$zip_path" | cut -f1 | tr -d ' '))"
  fi

  if [[ $DO_SERVE -eq 1 ]]; then
    say "Local smoke test"
    exec python3 tools/serve-web-build.py "$stage"
  fi
}

# ============================================================================ mac
stage_mac() {                                     # stage_mac <rid>
  local rid="$1"
  local publish="artifacts/mac/$rid"
  local stage="$STAGE_ROOT/$rid"
  local app="$stage/$APP_NAME.app"
  local min_os
  [[ "$rid" == "osx-arm64" ]] && min_os="11.0" || min_os="10.15"

  if [[ $SKIP_BUILD -eq 0 ]]; then
    say "Building $DESKTOP_PROJECT ($rid, self-contained)"
    rm -rf "$publish"
    dotnet publish "$DESKTOP_PROJECT" -c Release -r "$rid" --self-contained true -o "$publish"
  fi
  [[ -x "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" ]] || die "no $rid publish output at $publish — drop --skip-build"

  # Ad-hoc sign the executable BEFORE it goes into the bundle, and never with --deep.
  #
  # Apple Silicon refuses to execute an unsigned arm64 binary at all, so this is load-bearing on
  # osx-arm64 (x86_64 will run unsigned, but both are signed for consistency). The ordering is the
  # subtle part: codesign inspects the PATH it is given, and a target inside .app/Contents/MacOS makes
  # it adopt the whole bundle as the signing subject and walk everything beside the executable. Both
  # things it then finds there are fatal to it —
  #   * the raw art tree, where an animation is a DIRECTORY WITH AN EXTENSION ("Chest Open.anim", see
  #     Content/Art/MANIFEST.md), which it reads as a malformed nested bundle:
  #     "bundle format unrecognized, invalid, or unsuitable"
  #   * the managed assemblies, which are not Mach-O: "code object is not signed at all ... System.IO.dll"
  # Both have to live beside the executable, because the game resolves assets from BaseDirectory. So
  # sign in the plain publish directory, where the binary is just a lone Mach-O, and let cp -a carry the
  # signature in (it is embedded in the binary, so copying preserves it).
  #
  # This does NOT avoid the Gatekeeper prompt on a downloaded build — that needs a Developer ID and
  # notarisation. It makes the app launchable once the user allows it.
  local signed=0
  if command -v codesign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    codesign --force --sign - "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
      || die "codesign failed on $publish/$EXECUTABLE — an arm64 build will not launch at all"
    # Verify HERE, on the lone Mach-O, where codesign has no bundle to interpret. Asking it about the
    # copy inside .app/Contents/MacOS instead makes it adopt the BUNDLE as its subject (it reports
    # "Format=app bundle"), and it then walks the raw art tree beside the executable — the same
    # ambiguity that makes --deep unusable here. That check failed spuriously on a correctly signed
    # build; this one cannot, because there is nothing around the file to misread.
    # Captured into a variable, NOT piped into grep -q. See the pipefail note at the top of this script:
    # `codesign -dv … | grep -q …` fails spuriously under `set -o pipefail`.
    local signature
    signature=$(codesign -dv "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" 2>&1) || true
    [[ "$signature" == *"Signature=adhoc"* ]] \
      || die "codesign reported success but $publish/$EXECUTABLE is not signed"
    signed=1
  else
    note "codesign unavailable — skipping ad-hoc signature"
  fi

  say "Bundling $rid -> $app"
  rm -rf "$stage"; mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS"
  cp -a "$publish/." "$app/Contents/MacOS/"
  find "$app" -name '*.pdb' -delete

  # NSHighResolutionCapable is not cosmetic here: without it macOS runs the app at 1x and upscales the
  # whole window, which softens every pixel in a game whose entire look is exact integer pixel scaling.
  cat > "$app/Contents/Info.plist" <<PLIST
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>CFBundleName</key>                  <string>$APP_NAME</string>
    <key>CFBundleDisplayName</key>           <string>$APP_NAME</string>
    <key>CFBundleIdentifier</key>            <string>$BUNDLE_ID</string>
    <key>CFBundleExecutable</key>            <string>$EXECUTABLE</string>
    <key>CFBundlePackageType</key>           <string>APPL</string>
    <key>CFBundleShortVersionString</key>    <string>0.1.0</string>
    <key>CFBundleVersion</key>               <string>0.1.0</string>
    <key>LSMinimumSystemVersion</key>        <string>$min_os</string>
    <key>LSApplicationCategoryType</key>     <string>public.app-category.games</string>
    <key>NSHighResolutionCapable</key>       <true/>
</dict>
</plist>
PLIST

  say "Verifying $rid bundle"
  [[ -f "$app/Contents/Info.plist" ]] || die "Info.plist missing"
  [[ -x "$app/Contents/MacOS/$EXECUTABLE" ]] || die "Contents/MacOS/$EXECUTABLE missing or not executable"
  local arch_line
  arch_line=$(file -b "$app/Contents/MacOS/$EXECUTABLE")
  case "$rid:$arch_line" in
    osx-arm64:*arm64*) ;;
    osx-x64:*x86_64*)  ;;
    *) die "$EXECUTABLE is '$arch_line', which does not match $rid" ;;
  esac
  note "executable     $arch_line"
  if [[ $signed -eq 1 ]]; then
    # "Did the signature survive the copy?" asked as an exact byte comparison against the file we just
    # verified, rather than by re-interrogating codesign inside a bundle. A signature is embedded in the
    # Mach-O, so identical bytes IS a preserved signature — and cmp cannot be confused by the .app around it.
    cmp -s "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" "$app/Contents/MacOS/$EXECUTABLE" \
      || die "the bundled executable differs from the signed one — cp did not carry the signature in"
    note "signature      adhoc (verified pre-copy, bytes identical after)"
  fi
  local xnb
  xnb=$(find "$app/Contents/MacOS/Content" -name '*.xnb' 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  [[ "$xnb" -gt 10 ]] || die "only $xnb .xnb in the bundle — the MGCB content build did not run"
  note "content        $xnb built asset(s) + raw art for file: keys"
  note "bundle         $(du -sh "$stage" | cut -f1 | tr -d ' ')"
}

# ==================================================================== music preflight
# The licensed .ogg masters are gitignored (Content/ATTRIBUTION.md), and the content build stands
# tools/placeholder-track.ogg — 2s of silence — in for any that is absent so a fresh clone can build at
# all (Content/MusicPlaceholders.targets). That substitution is exactly the kind of failure this script
# exists to catch: the build SUCCEEDS, the upload works, and the game is mute. The build's GMTK0001
# warning says so, but a warning scrolls past in a wall of MSBuild output and a push does not.
#
# Checked BEFORE any build, so it costs seconds rather than a full three-channel package. Expected
# tracks come from Content.mgcb's own `#begin Music/` blocks — the same source the substitution reads,
# so a track added to the game cannot be missed here.
assert_real_music() {
  local manifest="Gmtk2026.Core/Content/Content.mgcb"
  local placeholder="tools/placeholder-track.ogg"
  local placeholder_hash="" track path missing=() silent=()

  [[ -f "$placeholder" ]] && placeholder_hash=$(shasum -a 256 "$placeholder" | cut -d' ' -f1)

  while read -r track; do
    path="Gmtk2026.Core/Content/$track"
    if [[ ! -f "$path" ]]; then
      missing+=("$track")
    elif [[ -n "$placeholder_hash" && "$(shasum -a 256 "$path" | cut -d' ' -f1)" == "$placeholder_hash" ]]; then
      silent+=("$track")
    fi
  done < <(sed -n 's|^#begin \(Music/.*\)$|\1|p' "$manifest")

  if [[ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 || ${#silent[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    die "the music in this tree is not shippable.
    ${#silent[@]} silent placeholder(s): ${silent[*]:-none}
    ${#missing[@]} absent (the build would substitute silence): ${missing[*]:-none}
    Restore the real tracks with tools/clip-music.py — Content/ATTRIBUTION.md records the master and
    the exact arguments for each one. A build with these in it is mute, and nothing downstream says so."
  fi
  note "music          $(sed -n 's|^#begin Music/||p' "$manifest" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') licensed track(s) present, none placeholder"
}

# ============================================================================ run
say "Preflight"
assert_real_music
[[ $do_web -eq 1 ]] && stage_web
if [[ $do_mac -eq 1 ]]; then
  for rid in "${MAC_RIDS[@]}"; do stage_mac "$rid"; done
fi

if [[ $DO_PUSH -eq 1 ]]; then
  [[ -n "$TARGET" ]] || die "--push needs --target <user>/<game> (or ITCH_TARGET)"
  command -v "$BUTLER" >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ -x "$BUTLER" ]] || die "butler not found at '$BUTLER'"
  [[ $do_web -eq 1 ]] && push_channel "$STAGE_ROOT/html5" "html5"
  if [[ $do_mac -eq 1 ]]; then
    for rid in "${MAC_RIDS[@]}"; do push_channel "$STAGE_ROOT/$rid" "$rid"; done
  fi
  say "Pushed: ${PUSHED_CHANNELS[*]}"
  for channel in "${PUSHED_CHANNELS[@]}"; do
    echo "    $BUTLER status $TARGET:$channel"
  done
else
  say "Packaged, not pushed"
  cat <<EOF
    Push with:
      tools/publish-itch.sh --skip-build --push --target roooliv/witch-v-necromancer

    Page settings butler cannot set (once per project):
      - Kind of project:  HTML   (else the web upload is offered as a download, not played)
      - Embed size:       1280 x 720
EOF
fi

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
serve-web-build.py — serve a staged web build the way itch.io serves it, so the upload can be
proven before it is public.

itch.io does not serve an HTML5 game from a domain root. It serves it from a per-build SUBPATH:

    https://html-classic.itch.zone/html/<build-id>/index.html

That single detail is the difference between a game that runs and a black screen, because every
asset Blazor fetches is resolved against <base href>. Serving the build from a local root (the
obvious `python3 -m http.server` in the stage dir) tests the one layout itch never uses, and passes
while the real upload is broken.

So this mounts the build under /html/<fake-build-id>/ and reports every 404 loudly. A clean run here
means the paths are right; it does not test itch's CDN, only our own output.

    python3 tools/serve-web-build.py artifacts/itch/html5
    python3 tools/serve-web-build.py artifacts/itch/html5 --port 8123

MIME types are set explicitly rather than left to the system: .wasm MUST be application/wasm or
WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming refuses the module, and Python's mimetypes database does not know
about .wasm on every version. itch.io does serve application/wasm correctly — this is here so a
local pass means the same thing a remote pass does.
"""

import argparse
import http.server
import os
import posixpath
import socketserver
import sys
from pathlib import Path

# The subpath shape itch uses. The id is arbitrary — what matters is that the game is NOT at /.
MOUNT = "/html/2846731/"

TYPES = {
    ".wasm": "application/wasm",   # load-bearing: instantiateStreaming validates this
    ".js": "text/javascript",
    ".mjs": "text/javascript",
    ".json": "application/json",
    ".html": "text/html",
    ".css": "text/css",
    ".png": "image/png",
    ".dat": "application/octet-stream",     # ICU data
    ".xnb": "application/octet-stream",     # built MonoGame/KNI content
    ".mdscene": "application/octet-stream",
    ".pdb": "application/octet-stream",
}


class Handler(http.server.SimpleHTTPRequestHandler):
    root: Path = Path(".")
    misses: list[str] = []

    def translate_path(self, path: str) -> str:
        # Strip the query/fragment and the mount prefix, then resolve inside the build dir only.
        path = path.split("?", 1)[0].split("#", 1)[0]
        path = posixpath.normpath(path)
        if path.startswith(MOUNT):
            rel = path[len(MOUNT):]
        elif path in (MOUNT.rstrip("/"), "/"):
            rel = ""
        else:
            # Anything outside the mount is exactly the bug this server exists to catch: a request
            # for /_framework/... means <base href> is absolute. Let it 404 and be logged.
            rel = path.lstrip("/")
        target = (self.root / rel).resolve()
        if not str(target).startswith(str(self.root.resolve())):
            return str(self.root)                      # refuse to escape the build dir
        if target.is_dir():
            target = target / "index.html"
        return str(target)

    def guess_type(self, path):
        ext = os.path.splitext(str(path))[1].lower()
        return TYPES.get(ext) or super().guess_type(path)

    def send_error(self, code, message=None, explain=None):
        if code == 404:
            Handler.misses.append(self.path)
            sys.stderr.write(f"\033[1;31m  404  {self.path}\033[0m\n")
        super().send_error(code, message, explain)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *a):
        pass                                            # only failures are interesting


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("build_dir")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8127)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    root = Path(args.build_dir).resolve()
    if not (root / "index.html").is_file():
        print(f"no index.html in {root}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    Handler.root = root
    socketserver.TCPServer.allow_reuse_address = True
    with socketserver.TCPServer(("127.0.0.1", args.port), Handler) as httpd:
        url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{args.port}{MOUNT}index.html"
        print(f"serving {root}")
        print(f"  at an itch-like subpath:  {url}")
        print("  404s (the failure this catches) print in red below. Ctrl-C to stop.\n")
        try:
            httpd.serve_forever()
        except KeyboardInterrupt:
            print(f"\n{len(Handler.misses)} 404(s)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	<Project>
2	  <!--
3	    MusicPlaceholders.targets — makes the licensed music OPTIONAL to build with, so that
4	    `git clone && dotnet run` works on a machine that has none of it.
5	
6	    THE PROBLEM. The five music tracks are licensed Epidemic Sound masters and this repo is public, so
7	    `.gitignore` excludes `Content/Music/*.ogg` (Content/ATTRIBUTION.md records every track's source and
8	    the exact clip-music.py arguments that re-derive it). But Content.mgcb has a `#begin Music/<name>.ogg`
9	    block for each one and **MGCB hard-fails on a missing input**:
10	
11	        error : The source file '…/Content/Music/ambient-calm.ogg' does not exist!
12	
13	    Five of those, so a FRESH CLONE COULD NOT BUILD AT ALL — not "built without music", could not build.
14	    That is a worse bug than silent music: it is the whole project being unusable by anyone but its owner.
15	
16	    THE FIX. Before the content build, copy `tools/placeholder-track.ogg` (2s of silence we generated
17	    ourselves — tools/build-placeholder-track.py) over any track that is absent, so MGCB always has an
18	    input. The build then WARNS, by name, about every track that is standing on silence.
19	
20	    WHY SUBSTITUTE RATHER THAN SKIP THE BLOCKS. Skipping is cleaner in principle — MGCB has no
21	    conditionals, but the music blocks could live in their own .mgcb that each head includes only when the
22	    files are there, and the runtime already survives a Song that fails to load (MediaPlayerMusicPlayer
23	    catches it). It was rejected on blast radius: for BlazorGL the KNI builder puts EVERY content
24	    reference in one output dir and one intermediate dir (`wwwroot/Content/`, `Content/obj/BlazorGL/`), and
25	    MGCB cleans output whose source is absent from the response file it was handed — so two .mgcb files
26	    sharing an intermediate dir invite each build to delete the other's work. Substituting an input needs
27	    nothing from either head's content plumbing, keeps ONE .mgcb as the content manifest, and is
28	    per-track rather than all-or-nothing.
29	
30	    THE THREE RULES THIS FILE OBEYS
31	      1. NEVER overwrite an existing file. The Copy below is conditioned on the destination not existing,
32	         so a real track — the case on the owner's machine and in every release — is untouched, and the
33	         build output is byte-identical to what it always was.
34	      2. Be LOUD, every build, not just the one that wrote the placeholder. The warning is driven by
35	         comparing each track's SHA256 against the placeholder's, so it fires just as reliably on the
36	         tenth incremental build as on the clone. A marker file beside each placeholder would have been
37	         the obvious alternative and is strictly worse: it is state that can go stale, and going stale
38	         means a silent release with no warning.
39	      3. Derive the track list from Content.mgcb. The `#begin Music/` blocks ARE the list of tracks the
40	         build needs; a second copy of it here would be one more thing to forget when a track is added.
41	  -->
42	
43	  <PropertyGroup>
44	    <GmtkContentDir>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)</GmtkContentDir>
45	    <GmtkContentManifest>$(GmtkContentDir)Content.mgcb</GmtkContentManifest>
46	    <GmtkPlaceholderTrack>$(GmtkContentDir)../../tools/placeholder-track.ogg</GmtkPlaceholderTrack>
47	  </PropertyGroup>
48	
49	  <!--
50	    Hooked on RunContentBuilder because BOTH heads have one: MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task (desktop) and
51	    the KNI builder (web) use the same target names. BeforeTargets runs after that target's
52	    DependsOnTargets, which is fine — nothing in the chain up to it reads the .ogg files; MGCB is the
53	    first thing that does, and it runs inside RunContentBuilder itself.
54	  -->
55	  <Target Name="SubstitutePlaceholderMusic" BeforeTargets="RunContentBuilder">
56	
57	    <ReadLinesFromFile File="$(GmtkContentManifest)">
58	      <Output TaskParameter="Lines" ItemName="_GmtkManifestLine" />
59	    </ReadLinesFromFile>
60	
61	    <ItemGroup>
62	      <!-- Two steps rather than one Include-with-transform: the filter has to batch over the LINES, and
63	           a transform in the same Include makes which item %() refers to ambiguous. -->
64	      <_GmtkMusicBegin Include="@(_GmtkManifestLine)"
65	                       Condition="$([System.String]::Copy('%(_GmtkManifestLine.Identity)').StartsWith('#begin Music/'))" />
66	    </ItemGroup>
67	    <ItemGroup>
68	      <_GmtkMusicTrack Include="@(_GmtkMusicBegin->Replace('#begin ',''))" />          <!-- Music/x.ogg -->
69	      <_GmtkMusicFile Include="@(_GmtkMusicTrack->'$(GmtkContentDir)%(Identity)')" />  <!-- absolute -->
70	    </ItemGroup>
71	    <ItemGroup>
72	      <_GmtkMissingMusic Include="@(_GmtkMusicFile)" Condition="!Exists('%(_GmtkMusicFile.Identity)')" />
73	    </ItemGroup>
74	
75	    <!-- A better failure than MGCB's five "source file does not exist", and the only way this target can
76	         fail at all: it names the one command that fixes it. -->
77	    <Error Condition="'@(_GmtkMissingMusic)' != '' AND !Exists('$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)')"

<Project>
  <!--
    MusicPlaceholders.targets — makes the licensed music OPTIONAL to build with, so that
    `git clone && dotnet run` works on a machine that has none of it.

    THE PROBLEM. The five music tracks are licensed Epidemic Sound masters and this repo is public, so
    `.gitignore` excludes `Content/Music/*.ogg` (Content/ATTRIBUTION.md records every track's source and
    the exact clip-music.py arguments that re-derive it). But Content.mgcb has a `#begin Music/<name>.ogg`
    block for each one and **MGCB hard-fails on a missing input**:

        error : The source file '…/Content/Music/ambient-calm.ogg' does not exist!

    Five of those, so a FRESH CLONE COULD NOT BUILD AT ALL — not "built without music", could not build.
    That is a worse bug than silent music: it is the whole project being unusable by anyone but its owner.

    THE FIX. Before the content build, copy `tools/placeholder-track.ogg` (2s of silence we generated
    ourselves — tools/build-placeholder-track.py) over any track that is absent, so MGCB always has an
    input. The build then WARNS, by name, about every track that is standing on silence.

    WHY SUBSTITUTE RATHER THAN SKIP THE BLOCKS. Skipping is cleaner in principle — MGCB has no
    conditionals, but the music blocks could live in their own .mgcb that each head includes only when the
    files are there, and the runtime already survives a Song that fails to load (MediaPlayerMusicPlayer
    catches it). It was rejected on blast radius: for BlazorGL the KNI builder puts EVERY content
    reference in one output dir and one intermediate dir (`wwwroot/Content/`, `Content/obj/BlazorGL/`), and
    MGCB cleans output whose source is absent from the response file it was handed — so two .mgcb files
    sharing an intermediate dir invite each build to delete the other's work. Substituting an input needs
    nothing from either head's content plumbing, keeps ONE .mgcb as the content manifest, and is
    per-track rather than all-or-nothing.

    THE THREE RULES THIS FILE OBEYS
      1. NEVER overwrite an existing file. The Copy below is conditioned on the destination not existing,
         so a real track — the case on the owner's machine and in every release — is untouched, and the
         build output is byte-identical to what it always was.
      2. Be LOUD, every build, not just the one that wrote the placeholder. The warning is driven by
         comparing each track's SHA256 against the placeholder's, so it fires just as reliably on the
         tenth incremental build as on the clone. A marker file beside each placeholder would have been
         the obvious alternative and is strictly worse: it is state that can go stale, and going stale
         means a silent release with no warning.
      3. Derive the track list from Content.mgcb. The `#begin Music/` blocks ARE the list of tracks the
         build needs; a second copy of it here would be one more thing to forget when a track is added.
  -->

  <PropertyGroup>
    <GmtkContentDir>$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)</GmtkContentDir>
    <GmtkContentManifest>$(GmtkContentDir)Content.mgcb</GmtkContentManifest>
    <GmtkPlaceholderTrack>$(GmtkContentDir)../../tools/placeholder-track.ogg</GmtkPlaceholderTrack>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <!--
    Hooked on RunContentBuilder because BOTH heads have one: MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task (desktop) and
    the KNI builder (web) use the same target names. BeforeTargets runs after that target's
    DependsOnTargets, which is fine — nothing in the chain up to it reads the .ogg files; MGCB is the
    first thing that does, and it runs inside RunContentBuilder itself.
  -->
  <Target Name="SubstitutePlaceholderMusic" BeforeTargets="RunContentBuilder">

    <ReadLinesFromFile File="$(GmtkContentManifest)">
      <Output TaskParameter="Lines" ItemName="_GmtkManifestLine" />
    </ReadLinesFromFile>

    <ItemGroup>
      <!-- Two steps rather than one Include-with-transform: the filter has to batch over the LINES, and
           a transform in the same Include makes which item %() refers to ambiguous. -->
      <_GmtkMusicBegin Include="@(_GmtkManifestLine)"
                       Condition="$([System.String]::Copy('%(_GmtkManifestLine.Identity)').StartsWith('#begin Music/'))" />
    </ItemGroup>
    <ItemGroup>
      <_GmtkMusicTrack Include="@(_GmtkMusicBegin->Replace('#begin ',''))" />          <!-- Music/x.ogg -->
      <_GmtkMusicFile Include="@(_GmtkMusicTrack->'$(GmtkContentDir)%(Identity)')" />  <!-- absolute -->
    </ItemGroup>
    <ItemGroup>
      <_GmtkMissingMusic Include="@(_GmtkMusicFile)" Condition="!Exists('%(_GmtkMusicFile.Identity)')" />
    </ItemGroup>

    <!-- A better failure than MGCB's five "source file does not exist", and the only way this target can
         fail at all: it names the one command that fixes it. -->
    <Error Condition="'@(_GmtkMissingMusic)' != '' AND !Exists('$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)')"
           Code="GMTK0002"
           Text="Music tracks are missing (@(_GmtkMissingMusic->'%(Filename)', ', ')) and so is the silent stand-in tools/placeholder-track.ogg. Regenerate it with: python3 tools/build-placeholder-track.py" />

    <!-- SourceFiles is the placeholder repeated once per destination: Copy demands the two lists be the
         same length, and the transform is how you say "this one file, to all of these". -->
    <Copy SourceFiles="@(_GmtkMissingMusic->'$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)')" DestinationFiles="@(_GmtkMissingMusic)"
          Condition="'@(_GmtkMissingMusic)' != ''" />

    <!-- Every expected track exists by now, so this one comparison covers both the placeholders just
         written and any written by an earlier build. Hashing ~13 MB of real music costs a few ms. -->
    <GetFileHash Files="$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)" Algorithm="SHA256"
                 Condition="Exists('$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)')">
      <Output TaskParameter="Hash" PropertyName="_GmtkPlaceholderHash" />
    </GetFileHash>
    <GetFileHash Files="@(_GmtkMusicFile)" Algorithm="SHA256" Condition="'$(_GmtkPlaceholderHash)' != ''">
      <Output TaskParameter="Items" ItemName="_GmtkHashedMusic" />
    </GetFileHash>
    <ItemGroup>
      <_GmtkPlaceholderMusic Include="@(_GmtkHashedMusic)"
                             Condition="'%(_GmtkHashedMusic.FileHash)' == '$(_GmtkPlaceholderHash)'" />
    </ItemGroup>

    <Warning Condition="'@(_GmtkPlaceholderMusic)' != ''"
             Code="GMTK0001"
             Text="SILENT PLACEHOLDER music: @(_GmtkPlaceholderMusic->'%(Filename)', ', '). The licensed .ogg masters are not in Gmtk2026.Core/Content/Music, so the build substituted tools/placeholder-track.ogg to keep MGCB happy — the game builds and runs, those tracks are silence. DO NOT SHIP THIS BUILD: restore the real tracks with tools/clip-music.py (arguments per track are in Content/ATTRIBUTION.md)." />

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
build-placeholder-track.py — bake `tools/placeholder-track.ogg`, the silent stand-in the content build
substitutes for a licensed music track that is not on this machine.

    python3 tools/build-placeholder-track.py

WHY THIS EXISTS
The five music tracks are licensed Epidemic Sound masters and this repo is public, so
`Content/Music/*.ogg` is gitignored (see Content/ATTRIBUTION.md). But `Content.mgcb` has a
`#begin Music/<name>.ogg` block for each of them and **MGCB hard-fails on a missing input** — five
`The source file '…ambient-calm.ogg' does not exist!` errors — so a fresh clone could not build the
content at all, let alone run. `Content/MusicPlaceholders.targets` fixes that by copying this file
over any track that is absent, so MGCB always has an input; the build then WARNS (GMTK0001) naming
every track it stood in for, and the game runs silent where that track would have played.

WHY IT IS COMMITTED RATHER THAN ENCODED DURING THE BUILD
Two reasons, and the second is the load-bearing one:

1. A valid .ogg needs a real encoder, and the only one we can count on is the ffmpeg MGCB itself
   bundles (`find_ffmpeg` below, reused from clip-music.py — the same binary that builds Songs). But
   that binary arrives with the `dotnet-mgcb` tool, which the content build restores *during* the
   build. Depending on it to produce the input to that same build is a chicken-and-egg the first
   build on a fresh machine should not have to win. A `Copy` needs nothing.
2. A COMMITTED file has a stable hash, which is how the build recognises a placeholder it wrote
   earlier and keeps warning about it. Encoding at build time would produce different bytes per
   ffmpeg version, and then "is this file real music or our silence?" would need a marker file
   beside it — extra state that can go stale, in exchange for nothing.

So the encoder runs HERE, once, and its output is 3.7 KB of silence we own outright — no licence, no
attribution, nothing to redistribute. Re-run this only if the file is lost or its shape must change;
a re-run changes the hash, which is harmless (the build re-derives it every time) but does mean any
placeholder already sitting in Content/Music stops being recognised as one. Delete those.

WHY SILENCE AND NOT A TONE
It is what a missing track should sound like. A placeholder beep would be worse than the absence it
stands for, and it would survive into a build somebody ships.

The silence itself is written by Python's `wave` module rather than by ffmpeg's `anullsrc`: MGCB's
ffmpeg is a minimal build (clip-music.py documents its muxer list) and generating input is a lavfi
feature we should not assume it has. Transcoding a .wav to vorbis is the one thing it certainly does
— it is exactly what SongProcessor uses it for.
"""

import importlib.util
import os
import subprocess
import wave

TOOLS = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(TOOLS)
OUT = os.path.join(TOOLS, "placeholder-track.ogg")

# Long enough that MediaPlayer's loop is not restarting a stream several times a second (it plays this
# with IsRepeating), short enough to stay a rounding error in the repo. Nothing hears it either way.
SECONDS = 2.0
RATE = 44100          # 48000 also works; what must NOT reach MGCB is loudnorm's 192kHz (see clip-music.py)
CHANNELS = 1


def _find_ffmpeg():
    """clip-music.py's own resolver — PATH first, then MGCB's bundled build. Loaded by path because
    the filename is hyphenated, so `import clip_music` cannot reach it."""
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        "clip_music", os.path.join(TOOLS, "clip-music.py"))
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.find_ffmpeg()


def main():
    ffmpeg = _find_ffmpeg()
    scratch = os.path.join(TOOLS, ".placeholder-silence.wav")
    try:
        with wave.open(scratch, "wb") as w:
            w.setnchannels(CHANNELS)
            w.setsampwidth(2)
            w.setframerate(RATE)
            w.writeframes(b"\x00\x00" * int(RATE * SECONDS) * CHANNELS)

        # -q:a 0 because there is nothing to preserve; silence compresses to almost nothing anyway.
        subprocess.run([ffmpeg, "-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y", "-i", scratch,
                        "-c:a", "libvorbis", "-q:a", "0", OUT], check=True)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(scratch):
            os.remove(scratch)

    print(f"wrote: {os.path.relpath(OUT, ROOT)}  {SECONDS:g}s silence  {os.path.getsize(OUT)} bytes")
    print(f"       ffmpeg: {ffmpeg}")
    print("     Content/MusicPlaceholders.targets hashes this file to recognise the placeholders it")
    print("     wrote, so a new hash un-recognises any placeholder already in Content/Music.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

157	   `MOUNT = "/html/2846731/"` (the id is arbitrary — what matters is that the
158	   game is *not* at `/`), strips the prefix in `translate_path`, refuses to
159	   escape the build dir, and lets anything **outside** the mount 404 on purpose:
160	
161	   ```python
162	   # A request for /_framework/... means <base href> is absolute.
163	   # Let it 404 and be logged — that is the bug this server exists to catch.
164	   def send_error(self, code, message=None, explain=None):
165	       if code == 404:
166	           Handler.misses.append(self.path)
167	           sys.stderr.write(f"\033[1;31m  404  {self.path}\033[0m\n")
168	       super().send_error(code, message, explain)
169	   ```
170	
171	   Successful requests are not logged at all — only failures are interesting.
172	   On Ctrl-C it prints the 404 count, which is the number you actually want.
173	
174	**MIME types are part of the test.** The server sets them explicitly rather than
175	trusting the host database, because `.wasm` **must** be `application/wasm` or
176	`WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming` refuses the module, and Python's `mimetypes`
177	does not know `.wasm` on every version. The table also covers the MonoDreams
178	content types so a local pass means what a remote pass means:
179	
180	```python
181	TYPES = {
182	    ".wasm": "application/wasm",           # load-bearing: instantiateStreaming validates this
183	    ".xnb":  "application/octet-stream",   # built MonoGame/KNI content
184	    ".mdscene": "application/octet-stream",# native levels, MGCB /copy:-bundled
185	    ".dat":  "application/octet-stream",   # ICU data
186	}
187	```
188	
189	That `.mdscene` line is MonoDreams-specific and load-bearing. A shipped game
190	boots **native scenes only** (`CORE_TENETS.md` §6): `LoadLevelRequest` probes
191	`Content/Levels/<id>.mdscene` and **fails loud** when it is absent — there is no
192	format fallback to degrade into. So a level missing from, or mis-served by, the
193	upload is a hard boot failure, and this server is where you find out.
194	
195	Wire it into the publish script so the smoke test is one flag:
196	`publish-itch.sh --only web --serve` stages, asserts, then `exec`s the server.
197	
198	---
199	
200	## 3. `ExcludeAssets="all"` on every content-pipeline `PackageReference`
201	
202	**Signature.** A shipped macOS build of a pixel-art game weighs **116 MB**, and
203	`Contents/MacOS/` contains `libassimp` (10 MB), `libfreeimage` (12 MB),
204	`ffmpeg`, `ffprobe`, `basisu`, `crunch`, and SharpDX's **D3D shader
205	compiler** — on a platform with no DirectX. Nobody notices until someone reads
206	the bundle, because a fat build is not an error.
207	
208	**Why it passes locally.** A head must reference the content-pipeline packages
209	so restore populates them, and by default a `PackageReference`'s assets **flow
210	into the project's output**. Those packages are the *authoring* toolchain: model
211	importers, texture compressors, audio transcoders — tools for **building**
212	content. A shipped game only ever **reads** `.xnb`. The excess is functionally
213	invisible: nothing crashes, nothing warns, the game runs fine. It is just a
214	third of your download.
215	
216	**Countermeasure.** Mark the pipeline packages **build-time only**. Per the
217	dependency-parity table in
218	[`web-targeting.md`](../web-targeting.md#dependency-parity-what-changes-per-backend),
219	that is two packages per head:
220	
221	```xml
222	<!-- Desktop head -->
223	<PackageReference Include="MonoGame.Extended.Content.Pipeline" Version="4.1.0" ExcludeAssets="all" />
224	<PackageReference Include="MonoGame.Framework.Content.Pipeline" Version="3.8.4" ExcludeAssets="all" />
225	
226	<!-- Web head — GeneratePathProperty because the head Imports the builder's .targets
227	     and passes /reference: paths straight out of the package -->
228	<PackageReference Include="nkast.Xna.Framework.Content.Pipeline.Builder" Version="4.2.9001"
229	                  ExcludeAssets="all" GeneratePathProperty="true" />
230	<PackageReference Include="KNI.Extended.Content.Pipeline" Version="6.0.0"
231	                  ExcludeAssets="all" GeneratePathProperty="true" />
232	```
233	
234	**Why the content build is unaffected — the mechanism that makes this safe.**
235	MGCB runs **out-of-process**. `MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task` invokes the
236	`dotnet-mgcb` tool, which carries its own pipeline; custom importers are handed
237	to it as `/reference:` paths resolved from the **NuGet cache**
238	(`$(NuGetPackageRoot)monogame.extended.content.pipeline/4.1.0/tools/...`), and
239	`restore` fills that cache whether or not assets flow into the project. The web
240	head does the same with `$(PkgKNI_Extended_Content_Pipeline)`-style path
241	properties — which is exactly why it needs `GeneratePathProperty="true"`
242	alongside the exclusion. Nothing in either content build reads the head's
243	output directory, so removing the assets from it costs nothing.
244	
245	**Verify it, don't assume it.** The failure mode of getting this wrong is a
246	content build that breaks *only from clean*, because a stale `Content/bin` hides
247	it. Clear the intermediate + output content dirs, rebuild, and confirm the
248	`.xnb` count is unchanged:
249	
250	```bash
251	rm -rf MyGame.Core/Content/bin MyGame.Core/Content/obj
252	dotnet build MyGame.Desktop -c Release
253	find MyGame.Desktop/bin/Release/net8.0/Content -name '*.xnb' | wc -l
254	```
255	
256	Measured on the reference game's `osx-arm64` publish: **116 MB → 91 MB**, with
257	both bitmap fonts still building. Note the residue — 91 MB is the untrimmed
258	self-contained .NET runtime, a different problem with a different fix.
259	
260	---
261	
262	## 4. Codesign the plain executable, before bundling it
263	
264	**Signature.** On Apple Silicon the `.app` does not launch at all — macOS
265	reports it as damaged, or it dies instantly with no window. Or the signing step
266	itself fails with one of:
267	
268	```
269	bundle format unrecognized, invalid, or unsuitable
270	code object is not signed at all ... System.IO.dll
271	```
272	
273	**Why it passes locally.** Your own `dotnet run` never goes through a bundle,
274	and the machine that built the binary trusts it. **Apple Silicon refuses to
275	execute an unsigned arm64 binary outright** — this is a hard gate, not
276	cosmetics — but you only meet it on a *copied* artifact. And the signing failure
277	above is an *ordering* fault that looks like a signing fault: `codesign`
278	inspects the path it is given, and a target inside `.app/Contents/MacOS` makes
279	it adopt **the whole bundle** as the signing subject and walk everything sitting
280	beside the executable. In a MonoDreams game, two things live there and both are
281	fatal to it:
282	
283	- **The raw art drop folder.** Assets referenced by `file:` AssetKeys are copied
284	  raw beside the executable (the game resolves from `AppDomain.BaseDirectory`; a
285	  bundle launches with `CWD=/`, so nothing may resolve relative to the working
286	  directory). An animation authored as a *directory with an extension*
287	  (`Chest Open.anim`) reads to `codesign` as a malformed nested bundle.
288	- **The managed assemblies.** `System.IO.dll` and friends are not Mach-O, so
289	  they are "code objects not signed at all".
290	
291	This is also why `--deep` is unusable here.
292	
293	**Countermeasure.** Sign **in the plain publish directory**, where the binary is
294	a lone Mach-O with nothing around it to misread, then let `cp -a` carry the
295	signature into the bundle — a signature is embedded in the Mach-O, so copying
296	preserves it:
297	
298	```bash
299	dotnet publish "$DESKTOP_PROJECT" -c Release -r "$rid" --self-contained true -o "$publish"
300	
301	codesign --force --sign - "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" \
302	  || die "codesign failed — an arm64 build will not launch at all"
303	
304	mkdir -p "$app/Contents/MacOS"
305	cp -a "$publish/." "$app/Contents/MacOS/"
306	```
307	
308	Then verify **pre-copy**, on the lone Mach-O — asking `codesign` about the copy
309	inside `.app/Contents/MacOS` reintroduces the same bundle ambiguity (it reports
310	`Format=app bundle` and walks the art tree), and that check has failed
311	spuriously on a correctly signed build. Confirm the copy separately with an
312	exact byte comparison, which cannot be confused by the `.app` around it:
313	
314	```bash
315	cmp -s "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" "$app/Contents/MacOS/$EXECUTABLE" \
316	  || die "the bundled executable differs from the signed one — cp did not carry the signature in"
317	```
318	
319	Ad-hoc signing does **not** avoid the Gatekeeper prompt on a downloaded build —
320	that needs a Developer ID and notarisation. It makes the app launchable once the
321	user allows it, which on arm64 is the difference between a game and a dead icon.
322	
323	While writing the `Info.plist`, set **`NSHighResolutionCapable`**. Without it
324	macOS runs the app at 1× and upscales the whole window, softening every pixel in
325	a game whose entire look is exact integer pixel scaling — a MonoDreams game
326	rendering at a virtual resolution is precisely that game.
327	
328	### The pipefail trap: a passing check that reads as failing
329	
330	This one costs a full debugging session and belongs in the same recipe, because
331	it is what a verification script does to *itself*.
332	
333	Under `set -o pipefail` (implied by the near-universal `set -euo pipefail`), a
334	**consumer that exits early** — `grep -q`, `head -n1`, `awk … exit` — closes the
335	pipe, the **producer dies of SIGPIPE (exit 141)**, and the pipeline reports
336	failure. So a *passing* check reads as a *failing* one. The reference script's
337	signature check did exactly this: it aborted a correctly signed build with "not
338	signed", and the same command run by hand (no `pipefail`) passed — which sent
339	the diagnosis chasing `codesign`'s bundle behaviour rather than the shell.
340	
341	**Capture output into a variable and match it**, or use a single process that
342	reads the file itself:
343	
344	```bash
345	# WRONG: grep -q closes the pipe, codesign gets SIGPIPE, pipefail reports failure.
346	codesign -dv "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" 2>&1 | grep -q "Signature=adhoc"
347	
348	# RIGHT: no pipe to break.
349	signature=$(codesign -dv "$publish/$EXECUTABLE" 2>&1) || true
350	[[ "$signature" == *"Signature=adhoc"* ]] || die "codesign reported success but the binary is not signed"
351	```
352	
353	The same reasoning is why recipe 1's `<base href>` extraction is a single `awk`
354	pass instead of `grep | head -1 | sed`. Any verification pipeline that ends in
355	an early-exiting consumer is suspect: audit for `| grep -q`, `| head`, and
356	`| awk '…; exit'`.
357	
358	---
359	
360	## 5. Prune Blazor's `*.br` / `*.gz` before uploading to itch
361	
362	**Signature.** Nothing breaks. The web upload is simply a third larger than it
363	needs to be, and every player waits for bytes no browser will ever request.
364	
365	**Why it passes locally.** `dotnet publish` emits **pre-compressed copies** of
366	the WASM bundle for hosts that negotiate `Content-Encoding` — the Blazor dev
367	server and most static hosts do, so locally the compressed variants are the ones
368	actually served and everything looks efficient. **itch does not negotiate
369	`Content-Encoding`**: the loader fetches the plain files, and the `.br`/`.gz`
370	siblings are dead weight sitting in the upload. It is a correctness-free
371	failure, which is why it survives every test you have.
372	
373	**Countermeasure.** Delete them at stage time, along with `web.config` (IIS
374	hosting config, meaningless on itch):
375	
376	```bash
377	cp -a "$WEB_PUBLISH/." "$stage/"          # trailing /. so index.html lands at the stage ROOT
378	pruned=$(find "$stage" -type f \( -name '*.br' -o -name '*.gz' \) | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
379	find "$stage" -type f \( -name '*.br' -o -name '*.gz' \) -delete
380	rm -f "$stage/web.config"
381	note "pruned $pruned pre-compressed file(s) + web.config"
382	```
383	
384	Measured on the reference game: **9.2 MB of a 28 MB upload → 19 MB**, by
385	deletion alone. Note the `cp -a "$src/." "$dst/"` idiom — the trailing `/.` is
386	what puts `index.html` at the stage **root** rather than nesting a directory,
387	which is recipe 1's first assertion.
388	
389	If you also zip for a manual dashboard upload, zip **from inside** the stage dir
390	(`cd "$stage" && zip -qr … .`) for the same reason: itch opens
391	`<root>/index.html` and nothing else.
392	
393	---
394	
395	## 6. Ship a committed placeholder for gitignored licensed content
396	
397	**Signature.** Two distinct failures from one cause, and the second is worse
398	than the first.
399	
400	1. **A public repo nobody can build.** A fresh clone fails the content build
401	   with `error : The source file '…/Content/Music/ambient-calm.ogg' does not
402	   exist!` — five of them in the reference game. Not "builds without music":
403	   **could not build at all**. Every contributor, every CI job, every agent that
404	   clones the repo hits a wall.
405	2. **A mute release.** Once you *do* paper over the missing inputs, the build
406	   succeeds, the upload works, and the shipped game is silent — with nothing
407	   downstream saying so.
408	
409	**Why it passes locally.** The owner's machine has the licensed masters, so both
410	failures are invisible there by construction. And **MGCB hard-fails on a missing
411	input** while having no conditionals and no globbing — the `.mgcb` is a literal
412	list of files that must exist. A gitignored asset plus a `#begin` block for it is
413	a build that only its author can run.
414	
415	**Countermeasure — three rules, and each one is load-bearing.**
416	
417	**(a) Substitute a committed placeholder for any absent input; never overwrite a
418	real file.** An MSBuild target hooked `BeforeTargets="RunContentBuilder"` (the
419	target name is the same for `MonoGame.Content.Builder.Task` and the KNI builder,
420	so **one file serves both heads**) copies a committed stand-in over anything
421	missing:
422	
423	```xml
424	<ItemGroup>
425	  <_GmtkMissingMusic Include="@(_GmtkMusicFile)" Condition="!Exists('%(_GmtkMusicFile.Identity)')" />
426	</ItemGroup>
427	<!-- SourceFiles is the placeholder repeated once per destination — "this one file, to all of these". -->
428	<Copy SourceFiles="@(_GmtkMissingMusic->'$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)')"
429	      DestinationFiles="@(_GmtkMissingMusic)" Condition="'@(_GmtkMissingMusic)' != ''" />
430	```
431	
432	The `Condition="!Exists(...)"` is the whole safety story: a real track — the
433	case on the author's machine and in every release — is untouched, and the build
434	output stays byte-identical to what it always was.
435	
436	Derive the list from the **`.mgcb` itself** (`sed`/`ReadLinesFromFile` over the
437	`#begin Music/` blocks), never from a second list in the target. The manifest
438	*is* the set of inputs the build needs; a copy of it is one more thing to forget
439	when an asset is added.
440	
441	Substituting an input beats the seemingly cleaner alternative of splitting the
442	optional blocks into their own `.mgcb`: for BlazorGL the KNI builder puts every
443	content reference in **one output dir and one intermediate dir**, and MGCB
444	cleans output whose source is absent from the response file it was handed — so
445	two `.mgcb` files sharing an intermediate dir invite each build to delete the
446	other's work. Substitution needs nothing from either head's content plumbing,
447	keeps one `.mgcb` as the manifest, and is per-asset rather than all-or-nothing.
448	
449	**(b) Warn on EVERY build, by hashing — never with a marker file.** The warning
450	must be as reliable on the tenth incremental build as on the clone, because the
451	build that ships is rarely the build that wrote the placeholder. Compare each
452	input's SHA256 against the placeholder's:
453	
454	```xml
455	<GetFileHash Files="$(GmtkPlaceholderTrack)" Algorithm="SHA256">
456	  <Output TaskParameter="Hash" PropertyName="_GmtkPlaceholderHash" />
457	</GetFileHash>
458	<GetFileHash Files="@(_GmtkMusicFile)" Algorithm="SHA256" Condition="'$(_GmtkPlaceholderHash)' != ''">
459	  <Output TaskParameter="Items" ItemName="_GmtkHashedMusic" />
460	</GetFileHash>
461	<Warning Condition="'@(_GmtkPlaceholderMusic)' != ''" Code="GMTK0001"
462	         Text="SILENT PLACEHOLDER music: @(_GmtkPlaceholderMusic->'%(Filename)', ', '). DO NOT SHIP THIS BUILD." />
463	```
464	
465	A marker file beside each placeholder is the obvious alternative and is
466	**strictly worse: it is state that can go stale, and going stale means a silent
467	release nobody was warned about.** The hash is derived from the artifacts
468	themselves every build, so it cannot desync. This is also why the placeholder is
469	**committed** rather than encoded during the build: a committed file has a
470	stable hash (and encoding it at build time would need the very `ffmpeg` that
471	arrives *with* the content build — a chicken-and-egg the first build on a fresh
472	machine should not have to win). See `build-placeholder-track.py`, which bakes
473	2 s of silence *once*, writing the samples with Python's `wave` module and
474	letting MGCB's bundled ffmpeg do only the transcode it certainly supports.
475	
476	Make the placeholder **silence**, not a tone. It is what a missing asset should
477	sound like; a placeholder beep is worse than the absence it stands for, and it
478	would survive into a build somebody ships.
479	
480	**(c) Gate the publish on it.** A warning scrolls past in a wall of MSBuild
481	output; a push does not. The publish script re-derives the same list from the
482	same `.mgcb` and **refuses to package** when anything is missing or hashes to
483	the placeholder — before any build runs, so it costs seconds:
484	
485	```bash
486	while read -r track; do
487	  path="Gmtk2026.Core/Content/$track"
488	  if [[ ! -f "$path" ]]; then missing+=("$track")
489	  elif [[ "$(shasum -a 256 "$path" | cut -d' ' -f1)" == "$placeholder_hash" ]]; then silent+=("$track")
490	  fi
491	done < <(sed -n 's|^#begin \(Music/.*\)$|\1|p' "$manifest")
492	```
493	
494	The failure message must name the **command that fixes it** and the file that
495	records how to re-derive each asset (the reference uses an `ATTRIBUTION.md` with
496	the master and the exact clip arguments per track). Same for the MSBuild
497	`<Error>` path when even the placeholder is gone: name
498	`python3 tools/build-placeholder-track.py`, don't make the reader deduce it.
499	
500	Nothing here is music-specific. Any gitignored licensed input a `.mgcb` lists —
501	music, voice, purchased art — takes the same three rules.
502	
503	---
504	
505	## The pre-push checklist
506	
507	For an agent packaging a MonoDreams game, in order:
508	
509	1. **Preflight, before any build** — every `.mgcb`-listed licensed asset is
510	   present and none hashes to the placeholder (recipe 6c).
511	2. **Build** — `dotnet publish MyGame.Web -c Release -p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web`
512	   (global `-p:`, so it flows through restore to `.Core`) and
513	   `dotnet publish MyGame.Desktop -c Release -r <rid> --self-contained true`.
514	   Build the desktop head at least once first: the web content build borrows
515	   native FreeImage/freetype from the cached `dotnet-mgcb` tool
516	   ([`web-targeting.md`](../web-targeting.md#macos--linux-native-lib-shim-required)).
517	3. **Stage web** — `cp -a "$src/." "$stage/"`, then delete `*.br`, `*.gz`,
518	   `web.config` (recipe 5).
519	4. **Assert web** — `index.html` at the root; `<base href>` present and
520	   **relative**; `_framework/blazor.boot.json` + `dotnet.native.wasm` present;
521	   `Content/` file count > 10; every `_content/**/*.js` shim referenced by
522	   `index.html` exists on disk (recipes 1, 2).
523	5. **Smoke-test web** — serve the *staged* dir at `/html/<id>/` and confirm
524	   **zero 404s** (recipe 2).
525	6. **Sign then bundle mac** — `codesign --force --sign -` on the **plain publish
526	   executable**, verify there via a captured variable (not a pipe), `cp -a` into
527	   `Contents/MacOS/`, then `cmp -s` the two (recipe 4).
528	7. **Assert mac** — `Info.plist` present with `NSHighResolutionCapable`;
529	   `Contents/MacOS/<CFBundleExecutable>` exists and is executable; `file -b`
530	   architecture matches the RID; `.xnb` count > 10 (recipes 1, 4).
531	8. **Push** — only behind an explicit `--push`, with a commit-stamped
532	   user version.
533	
534	Also confirm your `ExcludeAssets="all"` is in place (recipe 3) whenever you
535	touch a head's `PackageReference` list — it is the one recipe that is a *code*
536	change rather than a script step, and the only one whose regression is silent
537	even in production.
538	
539	## See also
540	
541	- [`docs/web-targeting.md`](../web-targeting.md) — the `.Core` + heads model,
542	  `$(MonoDreamsPlatform)`, the KNI content build, the `nkast.Wasm.*` shim
543	  version coupling, and the Reach render limits. Everything recipes 1–3 and 5
544	  package.
545	- [`docs/CORE_TENETS.md`](../CORE_TENETS.md) — engine-wide invariants; §6
546	  (native-only level load, fail-loud) and §9 (a scene is ship-ready exactly when
547	  it has zero `file:` AssetKeys) both have upload consequences.
548	- [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) — build/test workflow and OS setup.
549	- [`roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj) — the
550	  reference game these recipes were extracted from. Its
551	  [`docs/publishing-itch.md`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/docs/publishing-itch.md)
552	  is the game-side companion: channel table, itch page settings `butler` cannot
553	  set, and the measured sizes quoted above.

# Shipping: the six failures that only exist in production

A MonoDreams game is verified by `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, and the headless
Demos host. None of them can see the failure class this page is about, because
its signature is:

> **the build succeeds, and the defect only appears after upload** — on itch.io's
> CDN, inside a macOS `.app` bundle, or on someone else's clone.

Every one of these passes `dotnet build MonoDreams.sln`, passes
`dotnet test MonoDreams.Tests/`, and runs perfectly from `bin/`. What breaks is
the *layout* the artifact lands in, the *toolchain* that gets carried along with
it, or the *files a clone does not have* — none of which the compiler models.
You cannot unit-test your way to them; they have to be **known**, and then
**asserted by a script that runs before the push**.

The reference game **Witch v Necromancer**
([`roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj), public) paid
for all six the expensive way — a black-screen web upload, an app macOS called
damaged, a 116 MB Mac build for a pixel-art platformer, and a public repo nobody
could clone-and-build. This page turns that tuition into recipes.

**Nothing here lands in the engine.** Shipping is per-game: the artifact layout,
the bundle identifier, the itch target, the licensed assets. MonoDreams stays a
framework (`CORE_TENETS.md` §1) and the game repo owns its `tools/`. So each
recipe points at a **reference implementation to adapt**, living in a *game*
repo, never in `MonoDreams/`.

> **Read alongside:** [`docs/web-targeting.md`](../web-targeting.md) — the
> `.Core` + per-platform-heads model, `-p:MonoDreamsPlatform=web`, the KNI
> content build and its macOS/Linux native-lib shim. Recipes 1, 2, 3 and 5 are
> all about *packaging what that document builds*.

Reference implementations, all on `main`:

| File | Recipe |
|---|---|
| [`tools/publish-itch.sh`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/tools/publish-itch.sh) | 1, 4, 5, 6 (the publish gate) |
| [`tools/serve-web-build.py`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/tools/serve-web-build.py) | 2 |
| [`Gmtk2026.Desktop/Gmtk2026.Desktop.csproj`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/Gmtk2026.Desktop/Gmtk2026.Desktop.csproj) | 3 |
| [`Gmtk2026.Core/Content/MusicPlaceholders.targets`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/Gmtk2026.Core/Content/MusicPlaceholders.targets) | 6 |
| [`tools/build-placeholder-track.py`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/tools/build-placeholder-track.py) | 6 |
| [`docs/publishing-itch.md`](https://github.com/roo-oliv/gmtk-2026gj/blob/main/docs/publishing-itch.md) | the game-side writeup of all of it |

---

## 1. The publish script asserts every upload precondition

**Signature.** The upload is accepted, the build page loads, and the game does
not run: a black canvas with `_framework/*` 404s in the console; or it boots and
throws on its first `Load<Texture2D>`; or macOS says *"the application is
damaged and can't be opened"*.

**Why it passes locally.** Each of these is a property of the **artifact**, not
of the code. `dotnet build` type-checks C#; it does not check that
`<base href>` is relative, that `index.html` is at the upload root, that the
content build actually emitted anything, that the JS interop shim versions in
`index.html` still match the restored packages, or that a Mach-O's architecture
matches the RID it was published for. Nothing in the toolchain owns those
invariants, so nothing fails when they are violated.

**Countermeasure.** Write a publish script that **stages, asserts, and only then
pushes** — and make `--push` opt-in, so packaging is always safe to run. The
reference `publish-itch.sh` gates every channel behind assertions that map 1:1
to a failure it has actually seen:

```bash

base_href=$(awk 'match($0, /<base href="[^"]*"/) {
    s = substr($0, RSTART, RLENGTH); sub(/.*href="/, "", s); sub(/"$/, "", s); print s; exit }' \
  "$stage/index.html")
[[ -n "$base_href" ]] || die "no <base href> — Blazor cannot resolve _framework/"
[[ "$base_href" != /* ]] || die "<base href=\"$base_href\"> is ABSOLUTE — every _framework/ fetch will 404"

content_files=$(find "$stage/Content" -type f 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
[[ "$content_files" -gt 10 ]] || die "Content/ has only $content_files file(s) — the content build did not run"
```

**The content build is a separate MSBuild path from the C# compile.** On web
that path is KNI's builder plus the macOS/Linux native-lib shim documented in
[`web-targeting.md`](../web-targeting.md#macos--linux-native-lib-shim-required)
— a chain of copied native libs, staged pipeline DLLs, and a nested

produces nothing and **the C# build still reports success**. You get a green

The interop-shim check closes the trap `web-targeting.md` names explicitly: a

drift from the markup:

```bash

done < <(grep -o '_content/[^"]*\.js' "$stage/index.html")
```

matches the RID, its signature survived the copy (recipe 4), and the bundle
holds real `.xnb`:

```bash

case "$rid:$arch_line" in
  osx-arm64:*arm64*) ;;
  osx-x64:*x86_64*)  ;;
  *) die "$EXECUTABLE is '$arch_line', which does not match $rid" ;;
esac
```

  worked on the build page" is worth nothing if you cannot tell which tree
  produced it.
- **Run the cheapest gate first.** The music preflight (recipe 6) runs *before
  any build*, so a non-shippable tree costs seconds instead of a full
